impact: 8 of the 10 /api/v1 routes gated on commands.run verify the token's ability and the caller's organization membership, then execute on the host without ever calling the Server or Site policy: log-shipping enable/resync/disable, metrics install/probe/thresholds, and errors retry/remediate. An organization member holding a commands.run token can therefore install agents, enable log shipping, change alert thresholds and trigger remediations on a server their workspace role does not let them touch - org membership is not server access, which is exactly the distinction SitePolicy and ServerPolicy exist to make. run-command was the ninth and was fixed in T-008; that fix is the pattern for the rest. Verified by a full matrix over all 104 api/v1 routes: tenancy checks are present everywhere (no route is missing one), so this is specifically the policy layer.
resolution: Fixed in T-022: AuthorizesHostExecution adds the policy call to all 8 routes plus view-level gates on the 2 poll endpoints. Covered by tests/Feature/Api/HostExecutionAuthorizationTest.php.
title: Host-executing API routes check the token ability but never the user's authorization
